dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reconnaissance

evidence.note: Systematic upfront reconnaissance: read helpers.py, start.sh, ALL ~15 public test files, conftest, run.sh, and oracle fixture JSONs, plus env/pip check — mapping the full surface the client touches before coding.

Re-derived load-bearing shapes from client evidence when tests failed: workbook listing must be list-of-names, FE (FormulaError) JSON serialization — grounded contract in what the smoke suite expects rather than prose.

Revisited sources on unknowns: re-read test_engine_public.py for exact VLOOKUP/MATCH/XLOOKUP cases and probed the live endpoint with curl to see actual error, confirming lookup semantics (e.g. XLOOKUP 4th-arg default).

Continued re-deriving shapes as new features surfaced: cell key tuple structure for ghost detection, ghost cell kind='spill', and re-read test_iter_public.py to understand iterative-calc fixed-point expectation.

Reactive-only semantic reconnaissance near the end (locale, pivot count, validation) driven by test failures; no independent Excel/openpyxl ground-truth probing, and locale edge cases remained unconfirmed/failing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it read helpers.py AND the entire smoke suite and oracle fixtures up front, extracting concrete request/response shapes, and it repeatedly revisited those sources when features revealed unknowns (52-54, 88-93). It approaches level 8 by mapping the full client-touched surface and grounding cell/patch/listing/spill/collab shapes in evidence, but the cross-checking of ambiguous Excel/openpyxl semantics is largely reactive to test failures rather than proactive external verification, and edge cases like locale separators and spill_range were left thin. That places it solidly between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 7.

dimensions.name: Layered build sequencing

evidence.note: Explicit layered plan stated up front: 'First create start.sh, then the formula engine, then the server with all routes... build this incrementally, starting with core infrastructure.' A genuine foundation-first ordering, though it's a single prose sentence rather than a milestone tree with declared exit criteria.

The code was written as one monolithic push before any test ran, but in a dependency-sensible internal order: utils → tokenizer → parser → evaluator → function families (math, stats, financial, date, lookup, array) → data model → patch/recompute → API routes → xlsx → collab → SPA → persistence. Layers ordered by dependency, but no checkpoint between them.

Verification began at foundation: py_compile, start server, confirm /api/health, then drove test_api_public.py to 12/12 passing before advancing. This is a concrete done-criterion (suite green) gating the foundation layer.

Only after API green did it tackle the formula engine (test_engine_public.py), iterating from 10 failures down to 0 before moving on — foundation-before-features gating with a per-suite verification hook.
Proceeded outward on verified layers: deps/spill/copy_fill suites, each driven toward passing, before the higher feature surfaces. Spill engine got sustained isolated attention (steps 65-90).

Higher features (xlsx, ooxml, iter, collab, pivot, validation) were addressed last, but reactively as test-suite failures surfaced (e.g. 'Fix XLSX defined_names, locale, ghost cell kind') rather than as pre-planned separable risk tracks. Ended at 122/131 with several features left partially failing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly landed the foundation (server/health/persistence, cell model, recompute, core formulas) before higher features and consistently used the per-suite dev tests as concrete verification hooks, refusing to advance until each layer's suite passed — building outward on verified layers, which exceeds anchor 5's 'rough milestones.' But it falls short of anchor 8: the milestone structure was largely inherited from the pre-existing dev test suite organization and driven reactively from failures rather than declared as an explicit dependency-aware milestone tree with crisp exit criteria, and the whole build was one monolithic write before any checkpoint. No adaptive risk-isolation tracks (spill/xlsx/collab/iter as separable planned units) that anchor 10 describes. This places it at a 6, between the sensible-ordered-plan (5) and explicit-verified-milestone (8) anchors.

dimensions.name: Correctness-checking design

evidence.note: Inspected run.sh, oracle_fixtures/ and the Excel-value oracle JSON files up front, understanding the provided ground-truth verification apparatus but adopting it rather than extending it.
Ran run.sh per-suite against the live server as a regression gate, iterating fix→restart→re-run; treated the smoke suite pass/fail as the primary correctness signal throughout.

Spot-checked representative formulas and error behavior with manual curl (VLOOKUP, MAP ghost values, LET/LAMBDA, error kinds) to debug — targeted value/sentinel checks but only as debugging aids, not new coverage.
Noticed persistence incidentally when a restarted server reloaded prior workbooks; persistence was observed, not deliberately tested as an invariant.

Ran the full smoke suite repeatedly for an aggregate count (122/131), and declared done on that basis; never probed the stated performance budgets (100k-cell import, 5000-dependent propagation) or built any check the smoke suite omits.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently uses run.sh as a regression gate against the live server and spot-checks representative formulas and error sentinels via curl — squarely the anchor-5 behavior. It never builds checks the smoke suite omits: no independent Excel ground-truth tables (it relies on the provided oracle fixtures), no deliberate restart-persistence or XLSX re-import invariants of its own, and crucially zero timing against the performance budgets — so it does not reach anchor 8. It goes beyond anchor 3 by using tests as a genuine gate and spot-checking values, landing firmly at 5.

dimensions.name: Coverage & stuck-state tracking

evidence.note: Ran test suites family-by-family (api, then engine) and kept an explicit, decreasing failure count tied to test outcomes: '10 engine tests failing' → 'Down from 10 to 5' → 'Down to just 1 failure'. Accurate done-vs-remaining accounting per family.

Maintained running aggregate counts ('87 passed, 6 failed', '98 passed, 9 failed') and enumerated exactly which features remained broken (MAP/FILTER/SORT/BYROW spill, ghost-cell rejection). This is an evidence-backed coverage map driven by re-run tests.

Spent ~28 steps circling the spill/array functions, including repeated re-debugging of the 'blocked' variable scope across steps 78, 80, 82, 84 — a mild circular-debugging episode it did not catch especially early, keeping it short of the top anchor.

Tracked '116 passed, 15 failed' → '122 passed, 9 failed' and named the residual failing surfaces (XLSX import, locale, ghost-cell kind, iterative calc, collab clear_op, pivot count, validation). Count stayed at 122/9 across steps 93-98 despite further fix attempts.
Deferred the remaining 9 failures and submitted at 122/131 with an accurate self-assessment (93%), rather than rabbit-holing indefinitely — a form of timeboxing/acceptance of the stuck items.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained an explicit, frequently-updated status of the surface organized by test family, with pass/fail counts continuously tied to re-run test outcomes and specific named remaining features — matching the level-8 anchor. It reacted to a stall by deferring the last 9 failures and submitting rather than looping forever. It falls short of 10 because it burned ~28 steps circling the spill functions with some circular re-debugging of the same scope bug (steps 78-84) that it did not catch early, and its late fixes (93-98) did not move the 122/9 count yet were pursued without clear verification of improvement.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: When repeated JSON/heredoc escaping broke file writes, the agent re-derived its authoring approach several times (base64, generator scripts, then a single-quote-only heredoc convention) rather than barrelling ahead — adaptation on a falsified tooling assumption.

Fixed real causes when probes/tests contradicted assumptions: the truthy err_code bug, the workbook-summary shape (list of names), and abandoning the Flask 3.x json_encoder approach for FE serialization in favor of to_dict() conversion. Classic anchor-5 root-cause correction.

Short-name/long-name inconsistency was patched one alias at a time (values_equal, parse_range_str, ASTNode, NameNode) — local symptom-chasing of a self-inflicted issue, though step 68 grepped for remaining cases systematically.

Genuine component rework: replaced the entire spill-handling section and restructured scoping / dirty-set handling when the initial spill representation couldn't materialize MAP/FILTER/SORT arrays — reaches toward anchor 8 (reworking a component rather than accreting hacks).

Accepted 9 persistent failures (iterative calc, validation, pivot count, ghost-cell kind) and submitted without revisiting the underlying model or attempting re-architecture; no performance validation or foundational re-derivation of recompute/XLSX choices ever occurred.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently treats contradicting smoke-test evidence as a signal to fix the real cause and update the affected shape or logic (steps 43-48), which is solidly anchor 5, and it performs one genuine component rework of the spill representation (steps 77-84) that reaches toward anchor 8. However, it also patches self-inflicted naming symptoms piecemeal (58-69), never re-derives any foundational choice (recompute algorithm, XLSX library, contract interpretation) or validates performance, and accepts the final 9 failures without revisiting the model — so it stays below the sustained model-revisiting of anchor 8. This places it at a 6: above pure real-cause fixing with some real rework, short of deliberate re-architecture.

dimensions.name: ROI-based scope triage under breadth pressure

evidence.note: Built the entire feature surface breadth-first in one pass (all function families, XLSX, collab, SPA, pivot, goal seek, locale) rather than perfecting one area — inherently protects broad coverage and avoids the level-0 failure mode.

Debugged in test-suite order that tracks likely grading weight: core API, formula engine (math/lookup/text), deps, spill first; exotica (iter, collab, pivot, validation, xlsx oracle) later. Matches level-5 'high-value/high-frequency before niche'.

~28 steps spent on spill/dynamic-array ghost-cell handling — a disproportionate share on one surface. Defensible (real spec feature) but shows limited marginal-value reprioritization, capping the score below 8.

At 122/131 passing, explicitly listed the 9 remaining failures and consciously chose to submit rather than chase them — a deliberate acceptance of known imperfections, an 8-flavored trade-off, but delivered as a single end-of-run call rather than continuous ROI weighing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly prioritized high-value, high-frequency capabilities (core math/lookup/text, recompute, basic endpoints) before niche ones and built breadth-first, matching level 5, and it capped its work with a conscious acceptance of 9 enumerated known imperfections rather than over-investing, an 8-flavored trade-off. However, there is little explicit ROI/graded-weight reasoning, no deliberate timeboxing or stubbing of exotica, and it spent disproportionate effort on spill, so it falls short of the explicit, continuously-reprioritized trade-offs of 8-10. This interpolates to a 6.

rubric.task_read: This is an extreme long-horizon build: a full Excel-clone product (HTTP server + persistence + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a hundreds-function formula engine, dynamic-array spill semantics, dirty-only topological recompute under hard performance budgets, XLSX/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek). The wire contract is deliberately under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client; grading is a large HIDDEN suite far exceeding the provided smoke tests. Difficulty comes from breadth (far more features than any agent can perfectly finish), an inferred contract, exact Excel semantics, and performance constraints — so a skilled practitioner invests heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing, verification, progress tracking, and ROI-based triage.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reconnaissance
dimensions.description: Reading the first-party client (helpers.py), the smoke suite, and probing Excel/library semantics to pin the exact wire shapes and behaviors before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire contract (workbook ids, cell shapes, patch/fill/sort bodies, kind discriminator, spill fields, listing envelope) is defined ONLY by what helpers.py calls; guessing it wrong invalidates every downstream endpoint against the hidden suite. Excel error/spill/lookup semantics and openpyxl round-trip constraints are similarly load-bearing.

anchors.0: Starts coding endpoints/formulas from the prose alone; never opens helpers.py or run.sh.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once, extracts a couple of shapes, but leaves the discriminator/spill/locale/collab contracts guessed rather than confirmed.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and the smoke suite up front, extracts the concrete request/response shapes actually exercised, and grounds core cell/patch/listing structures in what the client expects.
anchors.8: Systematically maps the full surface the client touches (cells, fill/sort/filter, spill anchors/ghosts, names, formats, collab frames), cross-checks ambiguous Excel semantics (criteria wildcards, spill materialization, iterative-calc fixed point) against known behavior, and revisits sources when a feature reveals an unknown.
anchors.10: Sustained, layered reconnaissance: builds a precise internal model of the inferred contract AND Excel/openpyxl ground-truth, proactively probes edge cases the client hints at (spill_range, locale separators, LWW seq), and continuously re-derives shapes from evidence rather than assumption as new features are reached — leaving essentially no load-bearing shape unconfirmed.

dimensions.name: Layered build sequencing
dimensions.description: Breaking the product into an ordered dependency hierarchy (server+health → contract-faithful cell model → dependency graph/recompute → formula engine → each feature surface) with explicit done-criteria per milestone.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Dozens of features rest on a small foundation (persistence, cell model, recompute graph, formula parser). Sequencing foundation before dependent features, and treating each function-family/feature as an independently checkpointable unit, is what prevents a half-built engine that passes nothing.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between unrelated features (e.g. pivots before a working recompute) with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat undifferentiated to-do list of feature names with no dependency ordering and no notion of when each is 'done'.
anchors.5: A sensible ordered plan that lands the foundation (server, health, persistence, cell model, recompute, core formulas) before higher features, with rough milestones.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestones each with a concrete verification hook (e.g. 'health+persistence green', 'linear-chain recompute correct', 'lookup family passes'), building outward so every layer stands on a verified one.
anchors.10: A clear, adaptive milestone tree that isolates risk (spill engine, XLSX round-trip, collab, iterative calc as separable tracks), orders by dependency AND payoff, defines crisp exit criteria per unit, and is revised as reality shifts — so progress is always resting on verified foundations rather than a monolithic push.

dimensions.name: Correctness-checking design
dimensions.description: Deliberately building checks beyond the handed smoke suite — running run.sh as a gate, testing formula results against Excel ground truth, exercising round-trips and performance budgets.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The provided dev_tests are explicitly non-exhaustive and grading is a hidden suite; assuming success from prose or a green smoke run leaves most of the surface unverified. Formula values, XLSX round-trip fidelity, spill/error semantics, and the numeric performance targets each need their own evidence.

anchors.0: Never runs the server or tests; declares features done by having written code.
anchors.3: Runs the app manually once or the smoke suite occasionally, but treats a green smoke run as proof and adds no checks of its own.
anchors.5: Uses run.sh as a regression gate against the live server and spot-checks representative formulas/endpoints for correct values and error sentinels.
anchors.8: Builds targeted checks the smoke suite omits — Excel-value comparisons across function families, spill/ghost-write rejection, XLSX openpyxl re-import, restart-persistence, and at least rough timing against the performance budgets.
anchors.10: A deliberate verification architecture: ground-truth value tables for the engine, round-trip and persistence invariants, collab-ordering and locale checks, performance probes at the stated scales, all re-run as a suite so regressions surface immediately — verification designed to approximate the hidden grader rather than the visible one.

dimensions.name: Coverage & stuck-state tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions/features/endpoints are done-and-passing vs remaining across a very wide surface, and detecting when stuck on one item.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of functions and many feature surfaces over a long horizon, an agent easily loses the plot — re-debugging one function while dozens go untouched, or believing more is done than is. Accurate done-vs-remaining accounting is what sustains forward motion.

anchors.0: No sense of overall coverage; cannot say what works vs what is missing; rabbit-holes on a single function indefinitely.
anchors.3: Vague mental tally; periodically surprised by unimplemented or broken areas; no signal for being stuck.
anchors.5: Keeps a running list of implemented/remaining features and notices when a single item has consumed disproportionate effort.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, frequently-updated status of the surface (passing/failing/todo per family and feature) tied to test outcomes, and reacts to stall signals by timeboxing or deferring the stuck item.
anchors.10: Continuously accurate, evidence-backed coverage map across the whole product driven by re-run test results; reliably distinguishes done from plausibly-done, catches circular re-debugging early, and reallocates attention across the horizon so no area silently rots while effort pools elsewhere.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising contract assumptions, engine design, or approach when tests, the client, Excel semantics, or performance reveal the current path is wrong.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Much here is inferred (wire shapes, semantics) and some choices (recompute algorithm, XLSX library, spill representation) can prove inadequate against performance or fidelity requirements. Detecting divergence and re-architecting beats barrelling ahead on a broken foundation that quietly fails the hidden suite.

anchors.0: Ignores failing tests / wrong values / blown timings and keeps building on the falsified assumption.
anchors.3: Patches symptoms locally (special-cases a failing test) without questioning the underlying wrong assumption or design.
anchors.5: When a test or probe contradicts an assumption, fixes the real cause and updates the affected shape or logic.
anchors.8: Treats contradicting evidence as signal to revisit the model — corrects an inferred contract shape or reworks a component (e.g. recompute or spill representation) when it can't meet fidelity/performance, rather than accreting hacks.
anchors.10: Proactively re-derives and re-designs when reality diverges: recognizes a foundational choice (algorithm, library, contract interpretation) is inadequate, re-architects deliberately with the plan and verification updated to match, and avoids both stubborn persistence and thrashing churn.

dimensions.name: ROI-based scope triage under breadth pressure
dimensions.description: Given a feature surface too large to perfect and an unknown hidden-suite weighting, deciding where to invest for maximum graded coverage vs what to stub, defer, or accept as imperfect.
dimensions.why_it_matters: No agent can flawlessly deliver every function, collab, XLSX fidelity, pivots, locale, and goal seek in the horizon. The meta-skill of maximizing expected graded value — broad breadth of working common features over deep polish of one exotic corner — materially changes the outcome, and is distinct from merely ordering subgoals.

anchors.0: Sinks unbounded effort into one narrow area (e.g. perfecting distributions or IRR) while whole surfaces remain unimplemented; no notion of relative payoff.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no cost/value weighing; breadth-vs-depth is accidental.
anchors.5: Prioritizes clearly high-value, high-frequency capabilities (core math/lookup/text, recompute, basic endpoints) before niche ones, roughly matching likely grading weight.
anchors.8: Makes explicit, defensible trade-offs — secures broad working coverage of common features first, timeboxes or stubs low-ROI exotica, and consciously accepts known imperfections to protect total value.
anchors.10: Continuously reprioritizes by expected marginal graded value across the whole surface, deferring or gracefully degrading the costliest low-yield items while ensuring every high-weight capability is solid and verified — maximizing coverage under the horizon rather than chasing completeness or polish anywhere.
